legal/privacy/body.1: The data controller is **[COMPANY NAME — TO BE ADDED]**, VAT number [TO BE ADDED], based in 54033 Carrara (MS), Italy. For any privacy request you can write to mazzucchellipietro6@gmail.com.
legal/privacy/body.3:
- **Contact and request data**: name, email, phone, company, country and the content of messages sent through our forms (quotes, Marble Concierge, contact).
- **Booking data**: first and last name, email, phone, nationality, dates, number of participants, language, transfer and notes.

- **Photos uploaded to Marble Matching**: they are not stored. When AI analysis is active, the photo is sent to the service provider for the analysis only.
- **Technical data**: IP address, used for security and rate limiting, and technical server logs.
legal/privacy/body.4: ## Why we process them and on what legal basis
legal/privacy/body.5:
- Replying to requests and preparing offers: pre-contractual measures taken at your request (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
- Managing bookings, orders, payments and your account: performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)).
- Meeting tax and accounting obligations: legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)).
- Protecting the site from abuse and spam: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).
- Visit statistics: only with your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), which you can withdraw at any time from the cookie preferences.
legal/privacy/body.7: Data is processed by our authorised staff and, on our behalf, by technical service providers appointed as data processors: website hosting ([Vercel or Netlify — TO BE SPECIFIED]), database and authentication (Supabase), email delivery (Resend), payments (Stripe), spam protection (Cloudflare Turnstile), AI photo analysis (Anthropic, when active) and statistics ([Plausible or Google Analytics — TO BE SPECIFIED], only with consent). To organise experiences and supplies, we share with tourism partners and suppliers only the data that is strictly necessary.
legal/privacy/body.9: Some providers may process data outside the European Economic Area. In such cases, transfers are based on European Commission adequacy decisions or standard contractual clauses.
legal/privacy/body.11: We keep requests that do not lead to a contract for [TO BE DEFINED, e.g. 24 months]; contractual and accounting data for the period required by law (usually 10 years); account data until the account is deleted. Technical security logs are kept for [TO BE DEFINED].
legal/privacy/body.13: At any time you can request access to, rectification, erasure, restriction or portability of your data, object to processing and withdraw consent, by writing to mazzucchellipietro6@gmail.com. From your account you can also download your data and request deletion of the account. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (www.garanteprivacy.it).
legal/privacy/body.15: This notice may be updated; the version in force is always published on this page. This text is a starting point to be completed and reviewed by a legal adviser before publication.
legal/cookies/body.1: Cookies and similar technologies, such as the browser's local storage, are small files that the site saves on your device.
legal/cookies/body.3:
They are needed for the site to work and do not require consent:
- **wc_lang**: remembers your chosen language (12 months).
- **wc_auth** and **sb-…** (Supabase): keep you signed in to your account until you sign out or the session expires.
- **Browser local storage** (wc-consent, wc-lang, wc-selection, wc-compare, wc-collections): remembers your cookie and language choices, your marble selection, comparison and collections. It stays on your device only.
- **Cloudflare Turnstile**: spam protection for forms, loaded only on pages with a form.
legal/cookies/body.5: With your consent we enable statistics tools to understand how the site is used: [Plausible Analytics, which uses no cookies, or Google Analytics 4, which uses _ga cookies — TO BE SPECIFIED]. You can change your choice at any time from the “Cookie preferences” link in the footer.
legal/cookies/body.7: Online payment takes place on Stripe's secure pages, which apply their own privacy notice. The map on the Contact page is loaded from OpenStreetMap only after you click.
legal/cookies/body.9: You can also delete or block cookies from your browser settings; in that case some features, such as signing in to your account, may not work.

marbles/arabescato/tagline: Dense, interwoven veining, like a freehand drawing.
marbles/arabescato/description.0: Arabescato has a white background crossed by dense, interwoven grey veins that create a rich, lively pattern, which gives the stone its name.
marbles/arabescato/description.1: Some varieties look almost brecciated, with light areas enclosed by darker veins. It suits surfaces where character and movement are wanted.
marbles/arabescato/visualNotes.1: Dense grey and anthracite veins woven into a network, sometimes with a brecciated look.
marbles/arabescato/slabAlt: Slab of Arabescato marble with interwoven veining
marbles/bardiglio/tagline: The blue-grey of the Apuan Alps, understated and elegant.
marbles/bardiglio/description.0: Bardiglio is a grey marble, in shades ranging from light grey to blue-grey, crossed by darker veins that often run parallel.
marbles/bardiglio/description.1: It is the ideal choice for a natural material with a quiet character that pairs well with wood, brass and neutral tones. Commercial varieties differ in tone and pattern.
marbles/bardiglio/visualNotes.0: Grey background, from light grey to blue-grey.
marbles/bardiglio/visualNotes.1: Darker veins, often parallel, with thin light streaks.
marbles/bardiglio/slabAlt: Slab of blue-grey Bardiglio marble with linear veining
marbles/bianco-carrara/tagline: The classic white of the Apuan Alps, bright and versatile.
marbles/bianco-carrara/description.0: Bianco Carrara is the marble that made the city famous around the world: a white background with light grey shading, crossed by fine, evenly spread veins.
marbles/bianco-carrara/description.1: It is the best known of the Apuan marbles and suits very different projects, from contemporary architecture to classic interiors. Its look varies from block to block, so every supply is selected and approved together with the client.
marbles/bianco-carrara/visualNotes.0: White background with light grey shading, fairly uniform.
marbles/bianco-carrara/visualNotes.1: Fine, soft grey veins spread across the whole surface.
marbles/bianco-carrara/slabAlt: Slab of Bianco Carrara marble with fine grey veining
marbles/calacatta/tagline: A pure white background with broad grey and golden veins.
marbles/calacatta/description.0: Calacatta is recognisable by its warm white background and broad, irregular veins ranging from grey to golden or amber shades.
marbles/calacatta/description.1: It is a material with great impact, chosen for bathrooms, kitchens and prestige surfaces. There are many commercial varieties, differing in tone and pattern, so selection is made slab by slab.
marbles/calacatta/visualNotes.0: Warm white background, sometimes slightly ivory.
marbles/calacatta/visualNotes.1: Broad, irregular veins from grey to gold, with strong contrast.
marbles/calacatta/slabAlt: Slab of Calacatta marble with grey and golden veining
marbles/statuario/tagline: Intense white and bold veining: the marble of great works.
marbles/statuario/description.0: Statuario has a bright white background with sharp, dramatic grey veins. Its name recalls its historical use in sculpture, for which it was chosen for the purity of its background.
marbles/statuario/description.1: It is among the rarest and most sought-after marbles from the Carrara quarries and is used where the material must take centre stage. Availability, formats and prices depend on the blocks extracted and must always be checked before an offer.
marbles/statuario/visualNotes.1: Dark grey veins, sharp and striking, often broad and irregular.
marbles/statuario/slabAlt: Slab of Statuario marble with bold grey veining
experiences/esperienze-private/summary: A day built around you: quarries, art, food and landscape.
experiences/esperienze-private/descripti: For guests who want a private experience, we design days that combine quarries, workshops, culture and food, with dedicated guides and drivers.
Tell us your interests, dates and number of guests: we will propose a tailor-made programme, which becomes final only once the partners involved have confirmed.
experiences/esperienze-private/imageAlt: Guests with a guide on a panoramic terrace above the quarries
experiences/food-wine/summary: Lardo di Colonnata PGI and the wines of the Apuan hills, where they are made.
experiences/food-wine/description.0: A journey through local flavours, starting with Lardo di Colonnata PGI, cured in traditional marble basins.
experiences/food-wine/description.1: Alongside the lardo come products from Lunigiana and the Apuan coast and wines from the hills between Carrara and Massa, in tastings at selected producers and venues.
experiences/food-wine/highlights.0: Colonnata and the curing of lardo in marble basins
experiences/food-wine/imageAlt: Lardo di Colonnata on a marble board with a glass of wine
experiences/laboratorio-scultura/summary: Chisel in hand, guided by a sculptor.
experiences/laboratorio-scultura/descrip: A hands-on session in a sculpture studio: you learn about marble, the tools and the first gestures of carving.
Carrara has been a city of sculptors for centuries and is home to a historic Academy of Fine Arts. The workshop is led by professional artists, in small groups or privately.
experiences/laboratorio-scultura/imageAl: Sculpture studio with plaster models and a sculpture in progress
experiences/marble-workshops/summary: From block to object: sawmills and artisan workshops around Carrara.
experiences/marble-workshops/description: A tour of the companies that transform marble: sawmills, processing workshops and specialised craftsmen.
It is a chance to understand how a block becomes a slab, a worktop or a piece of furniture, and to see finishes and processing up close. Designed for architects, designers and enthusiasts.
From block to slab: cutting at the sawmill
experiences/marble-workshops/imageAlt: A craftsman's hands finishing a piece of marble
experiences/quarry-tours/summary: By off-road vehicle through the Carrara marble basins, among marble walls and views of the sea.
experiences/quarry-tours/description.0: An excursion into the marble basins of Colonnata, Fantiscritti and Torano, where marble has been extracted for more than two thousand years.
experiences/quarry-tours/description.1: You climb the quarry roads with authorised vehicles and operators, among white benches, freshly cut blocks and viewpoints that open onto the coast. The exact route depends on quarry activity on the day of the visit.
experiences/quarry-tours/highlights.0: The Colonnata, Fantiscritti and Torano basins
experiences/quarry-tours/highlights.2: Viewpoints over the Apuan Alps and the coast
experiences/quarry-tours/imageAlt: Off-road vehicle on a quarry road between walls of white marble
experiences/tour-panoramici/summary: Viewpoints over the Apuan Alps, among quarries, villages and the sea.
A scenic route along the roads that climb from Carrara into the Apuan Alps, with stops at the most spectacular spots, such as the Campocecina viewpoint, and in mountain villages.
On clear days the view stretches from the quarries down to the sea.
experiences/tour-panoramici/highlights.1: The mountain villages of the Apuan Alps
experiences/tour-panoramici/highlights.2: Views over the quarries and the coast
experiences/tour-panoramici/imageAlt: View from the Campocecina viewpoint over the quarries and the coast
experiences/transfer/summary: Private transfers to and from airports, stations, ports and hotels.
experiences/transfer/description.0: We arrange private transfers with professional drivers and premium vehicles, to reach Carrara or travel between the destinations of your tours.
experiences/transfer/description.1: Tell us your departure, arrival, date, number of passengers and luggage: you will receive a proposal once the availability of authorised operators has been checked.
experiences/transfer/imageAlt: Executive car with a driver in front of a historic building
experiences/visita-cava/summary: Inside a working quarry, with the people who work there every day.
experiences/visita-cava/description.0: A guided visit inside a quarry, open-pit or underground, organised with the owner or with authorised operators.
experiences/visita-cava/description.1: You see block cutting, the machinery and the quarrymen's work up close, in line with the quarry's safety rules. Visits take place only on the days and at the times agreed with the partner.
experiences/visita-cava/highlights.0: The quarry face and block cutting
experiences/visita-cava/highlights.1: The quarrymen's work and the safety rules
experiences/visita-cava/imageAlt: Inside an underground marble quarry with squared blocks
experiences/visite-culturali/summary: The historic centre of Carrara, between marble, art and history.
experiences/visite-culturali/description: A walk through the historic centre of Carrara: the Cathedral of Sant'Andrea with its marble façade and rose window, Piazza Alberica, the streets of the workshops and the places linked to sculptors.
On request, the visit can include the city's museums dedicated to marble and art.
The Cathedral of Sant'Andrea and its marble rose window
Piazza Alberica and the historic centre
experiences/visite-culturali/imageAlt: Marble façade of Carrara Cathedral with its rose window
destinations/capri/description.0: Capri is an island of limestone cliffs, gardens and villas. From the Piazzetta you reach the Gardens of Augustus, with their view of the Faraglioni rocks, and Via Krupp, which winds down to Marina Piccola.
destinations/capri/description.1: By boat you can sail around the island and, when the sea allows, enter the Blue Grotto. Anacapri and Villa San Michele complete the day.
destinations/capri/attractions.1: Gardens of Augustus and the Faraglioni
destinations/capri/experiences.0: Private boat trip around the island
destinations/capri/itineraries.0/text: Hydrofoil from Naples or Sorrento, boat trip, lunch and an afternoon between the Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus.
destinations/capri/imageAlt: The Faraglioni of Capri seen from the Gardens of Augustus
destinations/chianti/tagline: Hills, vineyards and villages between Florence and Siena.
destinations/chianti/description.0: Chianti is the quintessential Tuscan landscape: hills planted with vines and olive trees, cypresses, country churches and castles between Florence and Siena.
destinations/chianti/description.1: Villages such as Greve, Radda, Castellina and Gaiole are home to historic wineries and country restaurants, ideal for a day of tastings and views.
destinations/chianti/itineraries.0/text: Two winery visits with tastings, lunch in a village and a return at sunset along the Chiantigiana road.
destinations/chianti/imageAlt: Chianti hills with vineyards and cypresses
destinations/cinque-terre/tagline: Five colourful villages perched above the sea.
destinations/cinque-terre/description.0: Monterosso, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola and Riomaggiore overlook a stretch of coast shaped by vine terraces and dry-stone walls, a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with Portovenere and its islands.
destinations/cinque-terre/description.1: You can visit them by train, by boat (depending on the season) or along the National Park's trails. They are easy to reach from Carrara for a day trip.
destinations/cinque-terre/itineraries.0/: The Cinque Terre in one day
Train from La Spezia, three villages on foot, lunch with a sea view and a return by boat if the sea allows.
destinations/cinque-terre/imageAlt: The colourful houses of Manarola, in the Cinque Terre, above the sea
destinations/costa-smeralda/tagline: Granite, Mediterranean scrub and turquoise water.
In north-eastern Sardinia, the Costa Smeralda alternates coves of pale sand, wind-sculpted granite rocks and a sea of tropical colours.
Porto Cervo and Porto Rotondo are the centres of social life, while the La Maddalena archipelago is best discovered by boat.
Transfers to and from Olbia airport
Departure from Palau or Porto Cervo, stops in the coves of the La Maddalena archipelago, return at sunset.
destinations/costa-smeralda/imageAlt: Turquoise water and granite rocks on the Costa Smeralda
destinations/costiera-amalfitana/tagline: Roads above the sea, lemon groves and villages.
destinations/costiera-amalfitana/descrip: The Amalfi Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is one of the most spectacular landscapes in the Mediterranean: villages such as Amalfi, Ravello, Positano and Atrani overlook lemon terraces and a deep blue sea.
Amalfi is home to the Cathedral of Sant'Andrea, Ravello to Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone with their hanging gardens.
destinations/costiera-amalfitana/attract: Amalfi and the Cathedral of Sant'Andrea
Ravello: Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone
destinations/costiera-amalfitana/itinera: Positano in the morning, lunch in Amalfi, afternoon in the gardens of Ravello.
destinations/costiera-amalfitana/imageAl: The scenic road of the Amalfi Coast high above the sea
destinations/etna/tagline: The highest active volcano in Europe.
destinations/etna/description.0: Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You climb from the southern or northern slope up to altitudes where you walk among extinct craters and lava flows.
destinations/etna/description.1: High-altitude excursions take place only with authorised guides and may change depending on the volcano's activity. On its slopes, wineries produce increasingly acclaimed wines.
destinations/etna/itineraries.0/text: Drive up to Rifugio Sapienza, Silvestri Craters and, conditions permitting, the cable car; lunch at a winery.
destinations/etna/imageAlt: The craters and lava flows of Etna
destinations/firenze/tagline: The cradle of the Renaissance, among domes, bridges and masterpieces.
destinations/firenze/description.0: Florence holds some of the most important works of Western art. The historic centre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is best seen on foot: from the Cathedral with Brunelleschi's dome to the Ponte Vecchio, from the Uffizi to Michelangelo's David at the Galleria dell'Accademia.
destinations/firenze/description.1: With a private guide you skip the queues and also discover the artisan workshops of the Oltrarno.
destinations/firenze/attractions.0: Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore and Brunelleschi's Dome
destinations/firenze/attractions.4: Palazzo Pitti and the Boboli Gardens
destinations/firenze/experiences.0: Guided museum visits with booked entry
destinations/firenze/itineraries.0/text: Morning at the Cathedral and the Uffizi, lunch in the centre, afternoon between the Ponte Vecchio and the Oltrarno, sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo.
destinations/firenze/imageAlt: Brunelleschi's dome seen from Piazzale Michelangelo
destinations/genova/tagline: Palaces, alleys and the old port.
destinations/genova/description.0: Genoa was one of the great maritime republics. The Palazzi dei Rolli on Via Garibaldi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, tell of the wealth of its bankers and merchants.
destinations/genova/description.1: The historic centre is a maze of narrow alleys, the caruggi, that lead down to the Porto Antico, redesigned by Renzo Piano and home to the Aquarium.
destinations/genova/attractions.0: Via Garibaldi and the Palazzi dei Rolli
destinations/genova/experiences.0: Visit to the Palazzi dei Rolli
destinations/genova/experiences.1: Genoese street food in the caruggi
destinations/genova/itineraries.0/text: Via Garibaldi and the Rolli palaces in the morning, focaccia in the caruggi, Porto Antico and Boccadasse at sunset.
destinations/genova/imageAlt: The historic palaces of Via Garibaldi in Genoa
destinations/lago-di-como/tagline: Villas, gardens and villages on the water.
destinations/lago-di-como/description.0: Lake Como is famous for its historic villas on the water and for villages such as Bellagio, Varenna and Tremezzo.
destinations/lago-di-como/description.1: Villa del Balbianello, Villa Carlotta and Villa Melzi open their gardens to visitors, while ferries and private motorboats connect the shores.
destinations/lago-di-como/experiences.1: Visit to the villas and gardens
destinations/lago-di-como/itineraries.0/: Motorboat between Bellagio, Varenna and Tremezzo, a villa visit and lunch on the lake.
destinations/lago-di-como/imageAlt: A historic villa on Lake Como with its gardens
destinations/lago-di-garda/tagline: Italy's largest lake, among olive groves and castles.
destinations/lago-di-garda/description.0: Lake Garda combines Mediterranean landscapes with Alpine scenery. Sirmione, with the Scaliger Castle and the Grottoes of Catullus, stretches out on a peninsula in the south, while to the north the lake narrows between the mountains.
destinations/lago-di-garda/description.1: Its shores are home to villages such as Malcesine, Limone and Gardone Riviera, site of the Vittoriale degli Italiani.
destinations/lago-di-garda/itineraries.0: Sirmione in the morning, boat to Garda or Malcesine, sunset on the lake.
destinations/lago-di-garda/imageAlt: Sirmione and the Scaliger Castle on Lake Garda
destinations/lucca/tagline: The city within its Walls, to explore on foot or by bike.
destinations/lucca/description.0: Lucca is enclosed by perfectly preserved Renaissance Walls, today a tree-lined park to walk or cycle along.
destinations/lucca/description.1: In the centre you find Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, built on the remains of the Roman amphitheatre, the Guinigi Tower with trees on top and many Romanesque churches. It is also the birthplace of Giacomo Puccini.
destinations/lucca/itineraries.0/text: Morning in the centre and on the Walls, afternoon in the historic villas of the Lucca hills.
destinations/lucca/imageAlt: The tree-lined Walls of Lucca and Piazza dell'Anfiteatro
destinations/milano/tagline: Design, fashion and Leonardo's Last Supper.
destinations/milano/description.0: Milan is Italy's capital of fashion and design. The Cathedral, clad in Candoglia marble, dominates the square next to the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II.
destinations/milano/description.1: The refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie holds Leonardo's Last Supper, which can only be visited by reservation. The Fashion Quadrilateral and Brera complete the portrait of the city.
destinations/milano/itineraries.0/text: The Cathedral and its terraces, the Galleria and La Scala, the Last Supper in the afternoon, aperitivo in Brera.
destinations/milano/imageAlt: Milan Cathedral and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
destinations/napoli/tagline: Art, flavours and one of the most famous bays in the world.
destinations/napoli/description.0: The historic centre of Naples, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a maze of churches, palaces and alleys such as Spaccanapoli and San Gregorio Armeno. The National Archaeological Museum and the Sansevero Chapel, with the Veiled Christ, are not to be missed.
destinations/napoli/description.1: From the city you can reach Pompeii, Herculaneum and Vesuvius.
destinations/napoli/attractions.1: Sansevero Chapel and the Veiled Christ
destinations/napoli/attractions.3: Piazza del Plebiscito and the Royal Palace
destinations/napoli/experiences.0: Neapolitan pizza where it was born
destinations/napoli/itineraries.0/text: One day in the historic centre, one day between the ruins of Pompeii and Vesuvius.
destinations/napoli/imageAlt: The Bay of Naples with Vesuvius in the background
destinations/palermo/tagline: Mosaics, markets and the stories of many cultures.
destinations/palermo/description.0: Palermo bears the marks of Phoenicians, Arabs, Normans and Spaniards. The Arab-Norman route, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, includes the Cathedral, the Norman Palace with the Palatine Chapel and, just outside the city, Monreale Cathedral.
destinations/palermo/description.1: Historic markets such as Ballarò and the Vucciria tell the story of the city through its street food.
destinations/palermo/experiences.0: Street food in the historic markets
destinations/palermo/itineraries.0/text: Palatine Chapel and Cathedral in the morning, Ballarò market for lunch, Monreale in the afternoon.
destinations/pisa/tagline: Piazza dei Miracoli and a university city on the Arno.
destinations/pisa/description.0: Piazza del Duomo, known as the Square of Miracles, brings together the Cathedral, the Baptistery, the Camposanto and the famous Leaning Tower, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
destinations/pisa/description.1: Beyond the square, Pisa is a lively university city, with its riverside lungarni, Piazza dei Cavalieri and the Scuola Normale Superiore.
destinations/pisa/experiences.0: Climb the Tower with a timed ticket
destinations/pisa/itineraries.0/text: Piazza dei Miracoli with a climb of the Tower, then Piazza dei Cavalieri and the lungarni. Easy to combine with Lucca or with your return to the airport.
destinations/pisa/imageAlt: Piazza dei Miracoli in Pisa with the Leaning Tower
destinations/portofino/tagline: The piazzetta, the little harbour and the headland.
destinations/portofino/description.0: Portofino is a small fishing village that has become a symbol of the Ligurian Riviera, with its piazzetta overlooking the harbour and its pastel-coloured houses.
destinations/portofino/description.1: From the village you climb to the church of San Giorgio and Castello Brown, while the Portofino Park offers trails towards San Fruttuoso and its abbey by the sea.
destinations/portofino/itineraries.0/tex: Santa Margherita in the morning, a boat to Portofino and San Fruttuoso, aperitivo in the piazzetta.
destinations/portofino/imageAlt: Portofino harbour with its pastel-coloured houses
destinations/portovenere/tagline: The village on the headland, facing Palmaria Island.
destinations/portovenere/description.0: Portovenere closes the Gulf of Poets to the south: tower houses overlooking the harbour, Castello Doria and the church of San Pietro, perched on the cliff.
destinations/portovenere/description.1: Opposite lie the islands of Palmaria, Tino and Tinetto which, together with the village and the Cinque Terre, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
destinations/portovenere/itineraries.0/t: Lerici and Tellaro in the morning, ferry to Portovenere, boat trip around the islands in the afternoon.
destinations/portovenere/imageAlt: The church of San Pietro in Portovenere on the headland
destinations/positano/tagline: The vertical village of the Amalfi Coast.
destinations/positano/description.0: Positano cascades down to the sea, with pastel houses clinging to the rock and the majolica dome of the church of Santa Maria Assunta.
destinations/positano/description.1: Among boutiques, beaches and panoramic terraces, it is the ideal starting point to discover the coast by boat.
destinations/positano/experiences.1: Hike on the Path of the Gods
destinations/positano/itineraries.0/titl: Positano and the Path of the Gods
destinations/positano/itineraries.0/text: Morning hike from Bomerano to Nocelle, descent to Positano and an afternoon on the beach.

destinations/roma/tagline: Three thousand years of history in one city.
destinations/roma/description.0: Rome is an open-air museum: the Colosseum, the Imperial Forums and the Palatine tell of the grandeur of antiquity, while Baroque squares and fountains such as Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain bring the centre to life.
destinations/roma/description.1: A private guide lets you plan the visit with booked entries and tailor-made routes.
destinations/roma/attractions.4: Spanish Steps and Trinità dei Monti
destinations/roma/experiences.0: Guided visit of the Colosseum with booked entry
destinations/roma/itineraries.0/text: Ancient Rome on the first day, Baroque Rome and Trastevere on the second; the Vatican can be added as a third day.

destinations/siena/tagline: Gothic art, contrade and one of Italy's most beautiful squares.
destinations/siena/description.0: The historic centre of Siena, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, revolves around Piazza del Campo, with the Palazzo Pubblico and the Torre del Mangia. The Cathedral, with its inlaid marble floor, is one of the masterpieces of Italian Gothic.
destinations/siena/description.1: The city lives through its seventeen contrade, the protagonists of the Palio, run on 2 July and 16 August.
destinations/siena/attractions.1: Palazzo Pubblico and Torre del Mangia
destinations/siena/attractions.2: The Cathedral and its inlaid floor
destinations/siena/experiences.1: The Palio of 2 July and 16 August
destinations/siena/itineraries.0/text: The Cathedral and Piccolomini Library in the morning, lunch in the centre, afternoon between Piazza del Campo and the Palazzo Pubblico.
destinations/siena/imageAlt: Piazza del Campo in Siena with the Torre del Mangia
destinations/spiagge-sardegna/tagline: Some of the finest coastal spots in the Mediterranean.
destinations/spiagge-sardegna/descriptio: Sardinia offers miles of very different coastline: the pale beaches of the south, the cliffs of the Gulf of Orosei, the dunes of the west coast.
We help you build an itinerary through the coastal spots best suited to the season and to the way you travel, with transfers and services on request.
destinations/spiagge-sardegna/attraction: Gulf of Orosei and Cala Goloritzé
destinations/spiagge-sardegna/itinerarie: Excursion in the Gulf of Orosei among coves that can only be reached from the sea.
destinations/spiagge-sardegna/imageAlt: A beach of pale sand and crystal-clear sea in Sardinia
destinations/taormina/tagline: The Ancient Theatre between the sea and Etna.
destinations/taormina/description.0: Taormina overlooks the Ionian coast from a natural terrace. The Ancient Theatre, of Greek origin, offers one of the most famous views in Italy, with Etna in the background.
destinations/taormina/description.1: Corso Umberto, the historic palaces and the gardens of the Villa Comunale accompany your stroll; further down you reach Isola Bella.
destinations/taormina/itineraries.0/text: Morning on Etna with a guide, afternoon at the Ancient Theatre and dinner in Taormina.
destinations/taormina/imageAlt: The Ancient Theatre of Taormina with Etna in the background
destinations/vaticano/tagline: St Peter's, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel.
destinations/vaticano/description.0: The smallest state in the world holds immense treasures: St Peter's Basilica, with Michelangelo's dome and Bernini's colonnade, and the Vatican Museums, which culminate in the Sistine Chapel.
destinations/vaticano/description.1: The visit requires booked entry and appropriate clothing; an expert guide helps you find your way through the collections.
destinations/vaticano/attractions.1: St Peter's Square and Bernini's colonnade
destinations/vaticano/experiences.0: Guided visit of the Vatican Museums
destinations/vaticano/experiences.1: Climb to the dome of St Peter's
destinations/vaticano/itineraries.0/titl: Half a day at the Vatican
destinations/vaticano/itineraries.0/text: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel, then the Basilica and St Peter's Square.
destinations/vaticano/imageAlt: St Peter's Basilica and Bernini's colonnade
destinations/venezia/tagline: The city on the water, unique in the world.
destinations/venezia/description.0: Venice and its lagoon are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. St Mark's Square, the golden Basilica and the Doge's Palace are the heart of the city, while the Grand Canal flows between Gothic and Renaissance palaces.
destinations/venezia/description.1: The islands of Murano, Burano and Torcello complete the journey with glass, lace and the silence of the lagoon.
destinations/venezia/attractions.1: Doge's Palace and the Bridge of Sighs
destinations/venezia/experiences.1: Visit to the Murano glass furnaces
destinations/venezia/itineraries.0/text: First day around St Mark's, the Doge's Palace and Rialto; second day on the lagoon islands.
destinations/venezia/imageAlt: The Grand Canal in Venice with gondolas
destinations/verona/tagline: The Arena, the squares and the city of Juliet.
destinations/verona/description.0: Verona, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, combines Roman and medieval heritage: the Arena, still home to a famous summer opera season, dominates Piazza Bra.
destinations/verona/description.1: In the centre you pass Piazza delle Erbe, Piazza dei Signori and Juliet's House, while Castelvecchio and its bridge are reflected in the Adige.
destinations/verona/itineraries.0/text: Morning in the historic centre, afternoon at a Valpolicella winery.
destinations/verona/imageAlt: The Verona Arena on Piazza Bra
glossary/bacino-marmifero/definition: An area where several quarries are concentrated. In Carrara the main ones are Colonnata, Fantiscritti and Torano.
glossary/blocco/definition: A large rectangular piece of marble extracted from the quarry, from which slabs and worked elements are cut.
glossary/bocciardatura/definition: A rough finish obtained by striking the surface with a pointed tool, also used for exteriors.
glossary/cava-a-cielo-aperto/definition: A quarry where marble is extracted from the surface of the mountain, working down in benches.
glossary/cava-in-galleria/definition: A quarry where extraction takes place inside the mountain, carving out large underground chambers.
glossary/finitura-levigata/definition: A smooth but matt surface with a soft, natural look.
glossary/finitura-lucida/definition: A smooth, reflective surface that brings out colour and veining.
glossary/fondo/definition: The base colour of the marble, against which the veins stand out.
glossary/lastra/definition: A flat piece cut from the block, usually large, used for floors, cladding and worktops.
glossary/lizzatura/definition: An age-old technique for bringing blocks down from the quarry to the valley on wooden sledges, held back with ropes.
glossary/macchia-aperta/definition: Laying consecutive slabs from the same block opened like the pages of a book, so that the veins mirror each other (in Italian, macchia aperta).
glossary/resinatura/definition: A treatment in which resin fills small pores and micro-cracks in the slab.
glossary/retinatura/definition: A mesh applied to the back of the slab to support it during transport and installation.
glossary/sabbiatura/definition: A matt, slightly rough finish obtained with a jet of sand or abrasives.
glossary/scheda-tecnica/definition: A document listing the physical and mechanical properties of the material, measured in a laboratory according to specific standards.
glossary/selezione/definition: A set of slabs from the same block or similar blocks, chosen for uniform colour and pattern.
glossary/spazzolatura/definition: A finish obtained with abrasive brushes, giving the surface a velvety, slightly undulating feel.
glossary/spessore/definition: The depth of the slab, expressed in centimetres.
glossary/venatura/definition: A line or streak of a different colour from the background, caused by the presence of other minerals.
